alternatives.note: lower case for false gods: faalz gad

entries.note: Gad 3,763×; lexicon god → gad 87%. Gad is also the tribe Gad (REV 7:5): see questions.
Proposal: the LORD (YHWH) = di Laad, as the NT renders κύριος in OT quotations (MAT 4:7, MRK 12:29, HEB 8:8 "di Laad se"). project.yaml asks the team to decide the divine names.
YHWH Elohim (GEN 2:4 onwards) = di Laad Gad, as in REV 1:8, ACT 3:20 (14×).

entries.value: di Laad we a yu Gad
entries.note: "the LORD your God" is a relative construction: di Laad we a yu/unu/fi wi Gad (6× in quotations; MRK 12:29 "di Laad we a fi wi Gad").
God Most High (GEN 14:18–22) = di Muos Ai Gad (LUK 1:32, HEB 7:1).

entries.value: di Laad we av aal a di powa

alternatives.value: di Laad we ruul uova evriting
di Laad we muor powaful dan evri an eniting

entries.note: El Shaddai (GEN 17:1) and the Lord of Hosts have no single form; all are relative clauses about power (REV 1:8 "di wan we av aal a di powa").
Gad Spirit 39× (possessor first). GEN 1:2 "the Spirit of God" = Gad Spirit. Uoli Spirit = Holy Spirit.

alternatives.note: the visible sky, birds of the sky

entries.note: lexicon heaven → evn 77%, skai 6%. GEN 1:1 "the heavens and the earth" = di evn an di ort (2PE 3:5).
lexicon earth → ort 81%, worl 12%. Land of Canaan etc. = konchri (78×) or lan.
lexicon darkness → daak 48%, daaknis 34%; 2CO 4:6 "iina di daak" for GEN 1:3's quotation.
chrii = tree and three: context separates them.
Seed of plants = siid; seed as offspring = pikni (GAL 3:16 "tu im pikni").
lexicon descendants → pikni 88%; "pikni pikni" grandchildren (ROM 9:7).

alternatives.note: the dragon of Revelation, "serpent of old"

entries.note: created → mek (all 10 in the lexicon); κτίζω → mek 58% (occurrence index H1254). No separate word for create.
ruul uova (rule over).
kos (aaf) = curse (someone).
fried 98% for afraid; fear of God = rispek (fear → rispek 20%).
anger → beks 48%, wrath → beks 36%.
lexicon son → pikni 41%, bwai 34%. "Son of God" = Gad pikni (LUK 3:38).
give birth to a son = av (wan) bwai (pikni); be born = baan (ACT 7:8 "Aizak did baan").
No adjective: "she could not have (children)".
lexicon covenant → pramis 35%, plan 30%, diil 11%. pramis also renders "promise" and "oath": the team may want a separate word for בְּרִית.
burnt offering = bon … fi sakrifais (HEB 10:6 "bon uola animal fi sakrifais"); offering → sakrifais 47%, aafrin 16%.
temple → ous 77%, yaad 19%; "Gad ous" 131×.
No adjective: a righteous man = "sumadi we du wa rait" (HEB 11:4, 11:7). lexicon righteous → rait 36%.
Occurrence index H2617 (חֶסֶד): via ἔλεος, kain 51%, gud 10%; often "gud an kain tu". The team decides whether God's חֶסֶד needs a fixed phrase.
No fixed rendering: glory → brait 17%, priez 17%, big 16%, lait 11%. Shining glory = brait lait; honour = priez/rispek.
nation → piipl 44%, konchri 33%.
idols → faalz 53%; household gods (GEN 31) have no model: see questions.
faith → biliiv 35%, chos 30%: "chos iina Gad" (HEB 11:4–22) for trusting God.
nyam 222×; English "iit" is rare (99×).
Jussive commands of God: mek + subject + verb (Mek di lait shain, 2CO 4:6, God's word of GEN 1:3). "Mek lait de" (let light be) is built by rule.
Placed inside the quotation (HEB 8:8) or before it (ACT 7:49 "Di Laad se, ‘…’").
"(yu did av) wan man niem X" (10×); "we niem X" 37×; "we dem kaal X" 35×.
Genealogy: "<X> a did <Y> faada" or "<Y> a did <X> pikni" (LUK 3:34–38, MAT 1:2–3). For the Hebrew "X lived N years and fathered Y", combine with "av" (Iebriyam did av tuu bwai pikni, GAL 4:22).
JHN 1:1 renders "In the beginning" (an echo of GEN 1:1) so; "fram Gad mek di worl" = from the beginning of creation (MAT 19:4).

GEN 1:6 'wan big ruuf', then 'di ruuf'; 'di skai ruuf' for 'the expanse of the sky' (1:14-20); 1:8 names it Skai. Built on ruuf (roof, 7x). Footnote gives 'wan big kova'. Proposal for the team.
plit X fram Y (HEB 4:12 has 'plit op … fram'); shier means share, shiep shape.

entries.value: neva av no shiep, an it did emti
entries.note: Description in the corpus's explicit style; emti attested 3x (MAT 12:44, LUK 24:24, ACT 1:20).
תְּהוֹם; lexicon deep → diip 78%.
Piel participle מְרַחֶפֶת (a bird over its young, Deut 32:11): 'did a flai uova di waata' (past progressive). No NT model.
דֶּשֶׁא as the general category; esev = plaant, ets = chrii. tingz attested 178x, griin 4x.
עֵשֶׂב; lexicon plants → plaant 100%. 'evri griin plaant' (GEN 1:30).
Plants 'bier siid', trees 'bier fruut' (JHN 15:2, REV 22:2). The earth too: 'Mek di ort bier griin tingz' (GEN 1:11-12, by rule).
Doubled difrant (1CO 15:38) + kaina; used for every לְמִין in GEN 1. 'aal kaina' (ACT 11:6) for 'every kind'.
Of the waters (GEN 1:9-10): 'di waata we gyada tugeda'.
Niphal of ראה for the dry land: 'mek di jrai lan kom out' (GEN 1:9).
מוֹעֲדִים in GEN 1:14 (the appointed times); later feasts may want festival (GAL 4:10).

entries.note: biga (22x), likla (3x) comparatives.
נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה of animals; 'nof nof sitn we liv' for the swarms (GEN 1:20); 'evriting we av di bret a laif' (1:30).

entries.note: בְּהֵמָה as a class; no NT word. kou stays for cattle as cows.

entries.value: animal we kraal pan di grong
entries.note: JAS 3:7 has the GEN 1 list: wail animal, bod, animal we kraal pan di grong, animal we liv iina di sii. 'evriting we kraal pan di grong/ort'.
חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ = 'wail animal pan (di) ort'.
אָדָם generic in GEN 1:26-27: piipl (plural, so 'mek dem ruul', 'im mek dem'). 'man' would read as male only. Open: Adam as a name from GEN 2-5.

entries.source: בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ / in our image, after our likeness
entries.note: 'fi luk laik' (REV 13-16 for the beast's image) + 'fi bi laik' (1CO 11:7 per the wiki). GEN 1:27 'fi luk laik imself', 'fi luk laik Gad'.

entries.source: פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ / be fruitful and multiply
entries.note: Used for animals (GEN 1:22) and people (1:28). Birds: 'mek di bod dem ton nof nof' (1:22, juss. of רבה).
GEN 1:28 'tek kanchuol a it'; lexicon subdue → kanchuol.

entries.value: Iivnin kom, an maanin kom: dat a did di <ordinal> die.
entries.source: וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר יוֹם … / and there was evening, and there was morning, the … day
entries.note: Refrain of GEN 1 (5, 8, 13, 19, 23, 31): 'a did' as the past copula (LUK 3:34).
Naming: Gad kaal di lait “Die”; a fronted object keeps its place: an di daak im kaal “Nait” (GEN 1:5, 10).
